runs.t: Scalability is the ability to handle more load by adding resources or optimizing design. Elasticity is the ability to adjust allocated resources dynamically as load changes.

Differentiate vertical from horizontal scaling, throughput from latency, and resource utilization from queue depth. Autoscaling needs load indicators, warm-up time, limits and protection for databases and external dependencies.
An API can add replicas during seasonal booking spikes, but a shared database with an inefficient query may remain the bottleneck. Queue-based workers can scale by backlog when tasks are independent.
Autoscaling cannot compensate for serial bottlenecks or unbounded contention. Scaling out stateful workloads and cold starts often require a different plan from scaling stateless APIs.
